payload.prompt: Enviamos una factura por 18687 EUR a Solmar SL (org. nº 877276260) cuando el tipo de cambio era 10.33 NOK/EUR. El cliente ha pagado ahora, pero el tipo es 10.87 NOK/EUR. Registre el pago y contabilice la diferencia de tipo de cambio (agio) en la cuenta correcta.

payload.goal: Register payment of invoice for 18687 EUR from Solmar SL at current exchange rate 10.87 NOK/EUR, and post the foreign exchange gain (agio) arising from the rate difference (10.87 - 10.33 = 0.54 NOK/EUR) to the correct FX gain/loss account.
likely_resources: FX gain/loss account (typically account 8060 – Agio/valutagevinst in Norwegian chart of accounts)
Exchange rate at invoice date: 10.33 NOK/EUR
Exchange rate at payment date: 10.87 NOK/EUR
success_checks: Invoice of 18687 EUR is marked as fully paid
Payment registered at rate 10.87 NOK/EUR → NOK amount = 18687 × 10.87 = 203,147.69 NOK
Invoice was booked at 10.33 NOK/EUR → original NOK amount = 18687 × 10.33 = 193,036.71 NOK
FX gain (agio) = 203,147.69 - 193,036.71 = 10,110.98 NOK posted to account 8060 (Agio) or equivalent
Voucher/journal entry balances: debit bank 203,147.69 NOK, credit accounts receivable 193,036.71 NOK, credit agio account 10,110.98 NOK
Customer ledger for Solmar SL shows zero open balance after payment
risk_notes: Invoice date and payment date not explicitly provided — needed to confirm correct exchange rates in system
Tripletex may auto-calculate FX difference if multi-currency is enabled; verify that the system posts agio automatically or if a manual journal entry is required
Confirm which bank account received the payment (NOK or EUR account) — affects how FX difference is handled
If payment is received in EUR into a EUR bank account, the FX revaluation may need a separate voucher
Account 8060 (Agio) is standard in Norwegian chart of accounts; verify client's specific chart of accounts mapping
VAT not applicable to FX gain/loss posting
Organization number 877276260 should be validated against Brønnøysund/Spanish registry — format suggests Spanish CIF, not Norwegian org.nr
payload.suggested_first_action: Verify that multi-currency (EUR) is enabled in Tripletex under company settings, then locate the open invoice for Solmar SL (18687 EUR) and initiate payment registration with exchange rate 10.87 NOK/EUR.

line_items.description: FX gain (agio) – exchange rate difference 0.54 NOK/EUR on 18687 EUR → account 8060

ordered_steps: 1. Verify multi-currency module is enabled in Tripletex (Settings → Company → Currencies → enable EUR)
2. Ensure customer Solmar SL exists: POST /customer with org.nr 877276260, currency EUR
3. Locate or create the original invoice: GET /invoice?customerId={id} — confirm invoice amount 18687 EUR booked at rate 10.33 NOK/EUR (NOK 193,036.71)
4. Register payment: POST /invoice/{id}/payment with amount 18687 EUR, paymentDate = today, exchangeRate = 10.87
5. Confirm Tripletex auto-posts FX difference: check generated voucher for credit to account 8060 (agio) of NOK 10,110.98

6. If FX difference not auto-posted, create manual journal entry: POST /ledger/voucher — Debit bank account NOK 203,147.69 / Credit accounts receivable NOK 193,036.71 / Credit account 8060 NOK 10,110.98
7. Verify customer ledger balance for Solmar SL = 0 open items: GET /ledger/account?customerId={id}
8. Confirm voucher is balanced and posted in correct accounting period

Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD

payload.headline: Invoice created but payment registration failed to correctly record FX gain (agio) to account 8060
what_went_wrong: Only 1/4 scoring checks passed — the payment voucher likely did NOT correctly post the agio to account 8060 despite Tripletex generating 4 postings labeled 'Valutatap (disagio)' instead of 'Valutagevinst (agio)'.

The PUT /invoice/:payment call was made without verifying the body payload — the paidAmount and paidAmountCurrency fields may not have been correctly passed, causing incorrect FX difference calculation.
The agent assumed Tripletex auto-handled the agio posting correctly but never verified the actual account numbers in the 4 voucher postings — the FX difference may have gone to wrong account.
One 409 RevisionException error occurred on PUT /order due to stale version number, requiring an extra GET /order call to recover — avoidable with proper version tracking.
what_worked: Invoice creation flow (order → orderline → invoice) with EUR currency and rate 10.33 worked correctly.
Bank account 1920 configuration and EUR currency lookup were handled efficiently.
what_to_try_next: After registering payment, explicitly GET the voucher postings and verify account numbers — if agio is not on account 8060, post a manual journal entry: DR 1500 (AR) / CR 8060 (Valutagevinst) for the FX gain of 10,110.98 NOK.
Ensure PUT /invoice/:payment body explicitly includes paidAmount=203147.69, paidAmountCurrency=18687, paymentTypeId=37282700, and paymentDate to guarantee correct FX difference calculation.
Fetch the order version immediately after POST /order (before adding orderlines) to avoid the 409 RevisionException — or use the version returned in the POST response directly.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account (second call) — could have searched for account 8060 in the first call's results instead of making a second identical call.
GET /order/402036613 — avoidable if the version from POST /order response was used directly in the first PUT attempt.
GET /ledger/voucher + GET /ledger/voucher/609151021 — verification calls that didn't lead to corrective action when agio was posted to wrong account.
